text: During a Redis scale-up incident, connection failures increased because clients exhausted available connections. The team enabled graceful retries, increased connection pool limits, and verified backup replication before continuing the scaling operation.

metadata.title: Redis Connection Failures During Scale-up

text: A Redis failover test exposed stale replica data after a primary node failure. Engineers improved replication monitoring, added automated failover checks, and validated replica synchronization before promoting a standby.

metadata.title: Redis Failover and Replica Synchronization

text: Redis latency increased sharply after traffic was moved to a larger cluster. Analysis showed uneven key distribution and hot keys. The team rebalanced shards and introduced application-level controls for frequently accessed keys.

metadata.title: Redis Hot Keys After Cluster Expansion

text: A Kafka production outage occurred when brokers ran out of disk space because topic retention was configured too aggressively. The team removed obsolete data, increased storage capacity, and adjusted retention policies.

metadata.title: Kafka Outage Caused by Disk Exhaustion

text: Kafka consumers experienced delays during a traffic spike because several partitions had become heavily skewed. Engineers redistributed partitions and increased consumer capacity to reduce processing lag.

metadata.title: Kafka Consumer Lag During Traffic Spike

text: An API experienced intermittent timeouts when downstream database queries became slow. The mitigation included query optimization, connection pool tuning, and shorter request deadlines to prevent blocked requests from accumulating.

metadata.title: API Timeout Investigation and Mitigation

text: A sudden increase in API traffic caused request queues to grow rapidly. Rate limiting was introduced at the gateway, with separate quotas for internal and external clients to protect backend services.

metadata.title: API Rate Limiting During Traffic Surge

text: The authentication service returned intermittent unauthorized responses after a token signing key was rotated. The incident was resolved by synchronizing key configuration across service instances and improving key rotation procedures.

metadata.title: Authentication Failures After Key Rotation

text: Users were unable to log in after an identity provider configuration change. Engineers discovered that callback URLs were inconsistent between environments and corrected the redirect configuration.

metadata.title: Login Failure Caused by Identity Provider Configuration

text: A PostgreSQL database reached high CPU utilization during a reporting workload. Query analysis identified missing indexes and inefficient joins. Indexes were added and expensive reports were moved to an asynchronous processing queue.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL High CPU During Reporting

text: Database connections were exhausted when a new application release increased concurrent requests. The team reduced connection usage, corrected connection leaks, and configured safer pool limits.

metadata.title: Database Connection Pool Exhaustion

text: A Kubernetes deployment repeatedly restarted because the container exceeded its memory limit. Engineers reviewed memory usage, corrected a leak, and adjusted resource requests and limits after validating the workload.

metadata.title: Kubernetes Container Restart Due to Memory Pressure

text: A Kubernetes service became unavailable because readiness probes were too strict during application startup. The startup process was reviewed and probe thresholds were adjusted to allow sufficient initialization time.

metadata.title: Kubernetes Readiness Probe Failure

text: A load balancer distributed traffic unevenly because several backend instances were marked healthy despite elevated latency. Health checks were updated to include application-level readiness indicators.

metadata.title: Uneven Traffic Distribution Across Backend Servers

text: A cache invalidation problem caused users to see outdated product information after a deployment. The team changed cache keys, introduced explicit invalidation for affected records, and added tests for cache freshness.

metadata.title: Stale Data After Cache Invalidation Failure

text: An application deployment introduced a configuration value that was valid in staging but missing in production. The service failed during startup. Configuration validation was added to the deployment pipeline.

metadata.title: Production Startup Failure From Missing Configuration

text: A CI pipeline became slow after additional integration tests were introduced. Engineers parallelized independent test suites, cached dependencies, and separated fast unit tests from longer integration tests.

metadata.title: CI Pipeline Performance Optimization

text: A production service showed elevated error rates after a dependency released a backward-incompatible API change. The team pinned the dependency version, rolled back the deployment, and added compatibility tests.

metadata.title: Production Incident Caused by Dependency Change

text: Application logs became difficult to analyze because services used inconsistent field names and severity levels. A common structured logging format was introduced with standardized request IDs and error fields.

metadata.title: Standardizing Structured Application Logging

text: Monitoring failed to detect a service degradation because the existing alert tracked CPU but not request latency. The team introduced latency-based alerts and service-level indicators for availability and response time.

metadata.title: Improving Monitoring for Service Degradation

text: A backup restoration exercise showed that database backups were completing successfully but restoration had never been validated. The team introduced scheduled restore tests and documented recovery procedures.

metadata.title: Database Backup Restoration Validation

text: A message-processing service produced duplicate events after a consumer restarted. The team introduced idempotency keys and transaction-aware processing so repeated deliveries would not create duplicate business operations.

metadata.title: Preventing Duplicate Message Processing

text: A distributed service experienced cascading failures when one downstream dependency became unavailable. Circuit breakers, bounded retries, and fallback responses were introduced to prevent failure propagation.

metadata.title: Preventing Cascading Failures in Distributed Services

text: An internal integration failed because two services expected different versions of the same API contract. The teams introduced versioned endpoints and contract tests to detect incompatible changes before deployment.

metadata.title: API Contract Compatibility Between Services

text: A scheduled batch job missed its processing window because a long-running task blocked subsequent jobs. The scheduler was changed to run independent tasks concurrently and added execution-time monitoring.

metadata.title: Batch Processing Delay and Scheduler Improvements

text: A service became unavailable during a zone-level infrastructure failure. Traffic was redirected to healthy zones, and the architecture was updated to distribute critical workloads across multiple availability zones.

metadata.title: Service Recovery After Availability Zone Failure

text: An HTTP client generated excessive outbound requests because failed operations were retried without a limit. Exponential backoff and a maximum retry count were introduced to reduce pressure on the downstream service.

metadata.title: Controlling Excessive HTTP Retries

text: A search service returned inconsistent results after its index was rebuilt while documents were being updated. The team introduced versioned indexes and atomic index switching to avoid partially updated search results.

metadata.title: Consistent Search Results During Index Rebuild

text: A file-processing service slowed down when large uploads consumed all available worker threads. Engineers introduced upload size limits, asynchronous processing, and a queue-based worker model.

metadata.title: Large File Uploads Causing Worker Saturation

text: An incident review found that recovery took longer because operational runbooks were outdated. The team documented current rollback, failover, verification, and communication procedures and scheduled periodic reviews.

metadata.title: Improving Incident Recovery With Operational Runbooks
